extracted.intended_audience: public company legal counsel, CFO/CEO, investor relations, corporate secretaries, and audit committee members
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and legal requirements for preparing, disclosing, and publishing quarterly/annual earnings press releases and related conference calls/webcasts for publicly traded companies, with attention to SEC rules, listing standards, disclosure controls, and best practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form 8-K Trigger (Item 2.02)
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 2.02 of Form 8-K is triggered by the release of material, nonpublic information concerning the issuer's results of operations or financial condition for a completed fiscal quarter or year; once triggered the Form 8-K must be furnished to the SEC within four business days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies whether disclosure is oral (conference call/webcast) or written (press release). Item 2.02 is triggered only by historical (completed period) information — guidance about a future period generally does not trigger Item 2.02. A "preannouncement" made after the end of a completed fiscal period disclosing anticipated results will trigger Item 2.02. The Form 8-K furnishing requirement does not compel making an earnings announcement in advance of periodic report deadlines; it applies if an issuer elects to announce results earlier.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safe Harbor for Related Conference Calls / Webcasts
rubrics_metrics.description: If the press release is furnished on Form 8-K prior to a related conference call or webcast and the call is publicly accessible and occurs within 48 hours of the press release, oral disclosures during that call generally will not trigger an additional Form 8-K requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To satisfy the safe harbor, any additional financial/statistical information to be presented orally that was not in the press release also must be posted to the issuer's website prior to the call or the call must be simultaneously webcast. During the call the issuer must state where on its website the slide deck may be accessed. Subsequent disclosures of historical results outside these requirements would trigger a new Form 8-K.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form 8-K: Furnish versus File Considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: An issuer must decide whether to furnish or to file the Form 8-K; furnished material is publicly available but generally not automatically incorporated by reference into certain registration statements, whereas filed material is subject to automatic incorporation and potential additional liabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absent special incorporation concerns, it is generally better to furnish rather than file because Section 18 liability does not apply to merely furnished Forms 8-K; however, antifraud provisions such as Rule 10b-5 apply irrespective of furnishing vs filing. Companies may choose to file when ensuring that registration statements do not contain material omissions is necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulation G and Item 10(e) Requirement for Non-GAAP Numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: Any public financial disclosure that includes a non-GAAP number must be accompanied by and reconciled to the most closely comparable GAAP number; if the non-GAAP number appears in a document filed with the SEC, the additional restrictions of Item 10(e) of Regulation S-K apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reg G and Item 10(e) were adopted to prevent misleading non-GAAP disclosures. Non-GAAP measures can be useful if used transparently to enhance disclosure and comparability (e.g., highlighting core operating results). Reg G and Item 10(e) apply to both historical and forward-looking non-GAAP disclosures (unlike Item 2.02).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Non-GAAP Financial Measure
rubrics_metrics.description: A non-GAAP financial measure is a numerical measure of financial performance, position, or cash flows that excludes amounts included (or includes amounts excluded) under the most directly comparable GAAP number; it does not include operating/statistical measures or ratios calculated solely from GAAP numbers or operating/statistical measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Item 10(e) and Reg G share the same definition (textual nuances notwithstanding). The definition excludes operating measures such as unit sales or subscriber counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: GAAP Comparison and Reconciliation Requirement (core of Reg G / Item 10(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-GAAP numbers must be accompanied by and reconciled to the most closely comparable GAAP number, and even if reconciled the presentation must not contain an untrue statement of material fact or omit material facts necessary to avoid misleading investors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The general antifraud (Rule 10b-5) standard applies: reconciliation plus truthful, complete context is required. For oral disclosures, posting the GAAP reconciliation to the website by the time of presentation satisfies the reconciliation requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accommodation for Oral Non-GAAP Disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Verbal reconciliation on an earnings call may be ineffective; issuers may satisfy Reg G by posting the requisite GAAP information and reconciliation on the issuer's website prior to the oral presentation and disclosing the location during the presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The posting must occur by the time of the presentation and the location must be identified on the call. Many issuers meet this by posting the earnings release on the website prior to the call.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accommodation for Forward-Looking Non-GAAP Reconciliations
rubrics_metrics.description: When GAAP equivalent information and reconciliation for forward-looking non-GAAP measures is not available 'without unreasonable efforts,' the issuer must disclose that fact, provide any reconciliations available without unreasonable effort, identify the information that is unavailable, and disclose its probable significance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides relief for certain forward-looking measures (e.g., forecasts of core operating results when restructuring charges cannot be reasonably forecast). The issuer must be transparent about limitations and missing elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal or Greater Prominence of GAAP Numbers; Disclosure of Reasons for Non-GAAP Use
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 10(e)(1)(i) requires that GAAP comparison numbers be set forth with equal or greater prominence than non-GAAP numbers and that the issuer state the reasons why management believes the non-GAAP numbers provide useful information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical examples: report GAAP earnings per share prior to non-GAAP EPS; avoid highlighting non-GAAP achievements in the title/subtitle. The issuer should disclose (or include references to) the manner management uses the non-GAAP measure, the economic substance for using it, material limitations compared to GAAP, how management compensates for those limitations, and substantive reasons the measure is useful to investors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Prohibitions for Non-GAAP Information in Filed Documents (Item 10(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 10(e) imposes prohibitions when non-GAAP information is in a document filed with the SEC, such as: presenting non-GAAP numbers on the face of financial statements/notes; using confusingly similar titles to GAAP numbers; excluding cash-settlement charges from non-GAAP liquidity measures (except plain EBIT/EBITDA); adjusting supposedly nonrecurring items that are reasonably likely to recur within two years; and presenting non-GAAP numbers on the face of pro forma information under Article 11 of Reg S-X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although these prohibitions are specific to filed documents, following them for furnished earnings releases is advisable to avoid misleading presentations and SEC scrutiny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding Misleading Use of Non-GAAP Measures (general antifraud overlay)
rubrics_metrics.description: Even with reconciliation, presenting non-GAAP numbers that, together with accompanying information, contain an untrue statement of material fact or omit a material fact is prohibited under Rule 10b-5.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Companies should ensure reconciliations are complete and context is not misleading; SEC comment letters have required expanded disclosure and curtailed distribution of separate non-GAAP income statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forward-Looking Statements: Safe Harbor and Meaningful Cautionary Language
rubrics_metrics.description: Forward-looking statements must be identified as such and accompanied by meaningful cautionary statements that identify important factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from forward-looking statements in order to qualify for the PSLRA safe harbor (Section 21E).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Boilerplate, one-size-fits-all disclaimers are not recommended; case law (e.g., Asher v. Baxter) indicates specific, tailored cautionary language tied to the forward-looking matters and corresponding risk factors is important. Consider including a clear statement that the statements are as of the press release date and that the company does not assume any obligation to update them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to Update / Disclaimers About No Update Obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: Courts have divergent views on a post-disclosure duty to update forward-looking statements; publicly disclaiming a duty to update can help prevent a forward-looking statement from remaining 'alive.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended disclaimer example: state that statements are made as of the press release date and that the company does not assume an obligation to update the forward-looking statements to reflect subsequent events or circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure Controls and Procedures (DCP) Applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules require issuers to maintain disclosure controls and procedures (DCP), and for CEOs and CFOs to design, evaluate, and report on the effectiveness of those controls; DCP cover not only filed reports but also reports submitted/furnished to the SEC, including earnings releases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because DCP apply to submissions, issuers must adopt processes ensuring accuracy and timeliness for earnings releases: moving from ad hoc drafting to documented, well-planned procedures. CEO/CFO certifications in periodic reports carry personal liability if controls are ineffective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure Committee and Process Documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies are advised to form a disclosure committee (management-level, not a board committee) and to document processes and steps to be followed prior to public earnings disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested committee members include controller, general counsel/disclosure counsel, risk officer, chief investor relations officer, and business unit reps; many companies adopt smaller working groups with finance, legal, IR, and business unit leads. Use a documented Schedule of Actions (drafting, reviews, legal review, auditor involvement, audit committee review, finalization, distribution, EDGARizing, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit Committee Involvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Audit committees should exercise oversight of the accounting and financial reporting processes, including discussing earnings press releases and guidance as required by Nasdaq and NYSE listing standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The audit committee's charter should specify duties related to earnings releases; practice has been to have audit committee review and discuss each quarterly earnings release prior to dissemination. Meaningful audit committee involvement helps respond to heightened board/audit oversight expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulation FD Compliance and Means of Dissemination
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulation FD requires fair disclosure of material nonpublic information; compliant dissemination methods include press releases, public conference calls, webcasts, and Form 8-K filings (subject to exchange-specific rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nasdaq permits Reg FD-compliant disclosure via conference calls/webcasts; the NYSE continues to prefer/require a press release (and may require a press release no later than the start of the conference call/webcast). If material information is inadvertently disclosed on a call, the issuer must promptly issue a press release and notify the exchange if during market hours.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid Private One-on-One Communications of Material Information
rubrics_metrics.description: Private meetings, one-on-one calls, or invitation-only events conveying material nonpublic information risk violating Reg FD and have resulted in SEC enforcement actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: tone, emphasis, demeanor, or private statements that convey material information (Schering‑Plough); private investor meetings (Siebel); private 'ballparking' of estimates (Raytheon) — all can be actionable. Engage securities counsel for investor conferences and one-on-ones and avoid selective disclosures of material information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preannouncement Timing Rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Statements about anticipated results made during the fiscal period are typically forward-looking and do not trigger Item 2.02; however, a 'preannouncement' made after a fiscal period referring to anticipated results for that completed period will be treated as historical and trigger Item 2.02.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Careful assessment of timing and the nature (historical vs forward-looking) of statements is necessary to determine Form 8-K obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Earnings Press Release Schedule of Actions (Checklist & Timeline)
rubrics_metrics.description: A practical, multi-step timeline (exhibit) for preparing and issuing earnings releases and related conference calls, including drafting, reviews, legal/auditor working group reviews, audit committee review, finalization, EDGAR filing, exchange notification, issuance, website posting, and holding the conference call.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical actions and recommended timing include: prepare and issue press release/publicize call (T and T-7), collect/coordinate financial data, distribute first draft to working group (T-4), legal review of Form 8-K/Reg G/forward-looking disclaimers/Reg FD/Rule 10b‑5 (T-3), confirm/tick-and-tie financials, audit committee review (T-1), EDGARize and send to wire service (T), notify Nasdaq/NYSE at least 10 minutes before release, issue after market close, post release and materials on website, furnish Form 8-K with press release as exhibit after issuance and prior to call, hold call within 48 hours, maintain materials on website for at least 12 months (consider archival). Responsible parties and exact timelines should be documented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conference Call Materials: Posting and Access Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Slide decks and any additional financial/statistical information to be presented during a conference call must be posted on the issuer's website prior to the call if such information was not included in the press release (or the call must be simultaneously webcast) to satisfy Reg G and the Form 8-K safe harbor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The call script should identify where on the website the press release and supplemental materials (GAAP reconciliations, webcast link, any additional information) may be found. If materials are posted after a Q&A answer, they may be posted promptly but must still satisfy Reg FD and Reg G requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing Requirement: Furnish Form 8-K Prior to Conference Call
rubrics_metrics.description: The earnings press release should be furnished on Form 8-K after the press release is issued and prior to the related conference call to preserve the safe harbor for the call and to comply with Form 8-K timing obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that the Form 8-K is EDGARized and the press release included as an exhibit after issuance and before the call begins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insider Trading Window and Blackout Considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: The release of financial results will generally trigger the opening of the company's insider trading window if insiders are not aware of other material nonpublic information; insider trading compliance officers should notify insiders of the exact timing of window opening/closing or notify if the window will remain closed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider possible other blackout events (e.g., pending transactions) that may keep the window closed despite the earnings announcement; coordinate insider notices with the issuance/timing plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Website Retention and Archival of Release Materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Press release, conference call webcast and related presentations should be maintained on the company website for at least 12 months following the call, with consideration to move them to an archive/historical section prior to the 12-month mark.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain the materials to satisfy Reg G oral reconciliation accommodation and investor access; consider longer retention as appropriate for investor relations and compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal Review Items for Earnings Releases
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal review of draft press release, script and presentations should cover Item 2.02 furnishing/filing requirement, Regulation G and Item 10(e) non-GAAP issues, the statutory safe harbor for forward-looking statements and duty to update disclaimers, proper public notice for Reg FD and Item 2.02, factual backup, general disclosure, and Rule 10b-5 matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Involve auditors, internal finance, and external counsel as appropriate in the working group; incorporate comments and obtain final legal sign-off prior to issuance and Form 8-K furnishing.
